ImageDescription.value: Entering the Yarra Ranges National Park in Victoria from the north east. The location is close to the point where three river catchments meet. The Yarra River flowing into Port Phillip, the Thomson River part of the Latrobe River catchment that empties into Bass Strait and the Big River (Goulburn River) part of the Goulburn River catchment which flows into the Murray River and thence into the Southern Ocean in South Australia.

ImageDescription.value:
This magnificent sub-alpine rainforest is also home to 65 metre tall old-growth Mountain Ash trees, ferns, mosses and other plants that create this damp and diverse environment.

- Trees are the world's single largest source of breathable oxygen and play a vital role in addressing climate change. They filter air + provide oxygen, conserve soil + water, prevent desertification + protect/stabilise ground cover. -

The process of absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen is essential for the well-being of our unique planet, Earth. Look up to the trees for they provide us the air we breathe.
